tldr: Late-October papers attacked long-context cost from several sides: isolating context in chain of thought, initializing linear-attention memory, and learned sparse attention. By early November the work moved to production sparse attention, TPU kernels and agent-side context compression.
whats_new: Muir (Nov 5) reworks gated delta-rule linear attention with sensitivity-allocated gating, while QRAE compresses DeepSearch agent context using query-relevant attention entropy.
why_it_matters: Long-context cost drives inference spend and latency for agents. Sparse and linear attention variants, plus agent-level context compression, are the levers that decide how much context a deployment can afford.
take_for_builders: These are preprints with no shared benchmark, so do not plan around them yet. Track which ones ship in open-weight models or serving stacks, and rerun your long-context retrieval evals before adopting any.
